r0, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice, sIn));\n        dim3 grid((unsigned)std::min<size_t>((n + 255) / 256, 64), (unsigned)(r1 - r0));\n        zeroUpper<<<grid, 256, 0, sIn>>>(dA, n, r0);\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetLastError());\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaEventRecord(ctx.evChunk[c], sIn));\n    }\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaStreamWaitEvent(sUpd, ctx.evChunk[0], 0));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaStreamWaitEvent(sPan, ctx.evChunk[0], 0));\n\n    for (int c = 0; c < C; ++c) {\n        const size_t rEnd = R[c + 1];\n        const bool next = c + 1 < C;\n        if (c > 0) {\n            // Rows of this chunk have been caught up with all previous panels\n            CUDA_CHECK(cudaStreamWaitEvent(sUpd, ctx.evCatch, 0));\n            CUDA_CHECK(cudaStreamWaitEvent(sPan, ctx.evCatch, 0));\n        }\n        if (next) {\n            // Bring the next chunk up to date with all panels finished before this chunk\n            CUDA_CHECK(cudaStreamWaitEvent(sCat, ctx.evChunk[c + 1], 0));\n            if (c > 0) CUDA_CHECK(cudaStreamWaitEvent(sCat, ctx.evPanel, 0));\n            for (size_t kb = 0; kb < R[c]; kb += NB)\n                catchUpStep(ctx, sCat, kb, NB, R[c + 1], R[c + 2]);\n        }\n\n        for (size_t kb = R[c]; kb < rEnd; kb += NB) {\n            const int b = (int)std::min<size_t>(NB, rEnd - {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01BwceByEMu6WfQLcgeBoEoZ","type":"tool_result","content":"cholesky.cpp\nCMakeLists.txt\ncmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.24)\nproject(cholesky_benchmark LANGUAGES CXX CUDA)\n\nset(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20)\nset(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)\nset(CMAKE_CUDA_STANDARD 20)\nset(CMAKE_CUDA_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)\nif(NOT DEFINED CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES)\n    set(CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES native)\nendif()\n\nfind_package(CUDAToolkit REQUIRED)\n\n# The benchmark source is compiled as CUDA\nset_source_files_properties(cholesky.cpp PROPERTIES LANGUAGE CUDA)\nadd_executable(cholesky cholesky.cpp)\n\n# Enable optimizations\ntarget_compile_options(cholesky PRIVATE -O3 -Xcompiler=-O3,-march=native,-Wall,-Wextra)\n\n# Link CUDA runtime and math library\ntarget_link_libraries(cholesky CUDA::cudart m)","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"0662b794-5005-4748-a057-d5242925bb04","uuid":"ee1af74b-14cc-4bfb-b405-18c62e7b72c5","timestamp":"2026-10-05T04:01:37.120Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"cholesky.cpp\nCMakeLists.txt\ncmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.24)\nproject(cholesky_benchmark LANGUAGES CXX CUDA)\n\nset(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20)\nset(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)\nset(CMAKE_CUDA_STANDARD 20)\nset(CMAKE_CUDA_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)\nif(NOT DEFINED CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES)\n    set(CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES native)\nendif()\n\nfind_package(CUDAToolkit REQUIRED)\n\n# The benchmark source is compiled as CUDA\nset_source_files_properties(cholesky.cpp PROPERTIES LANGUAGE CUDA)\nadd_executable(cholesky cholesky.cpp)\n\n# Enable optimizations\ntarget_compile_options(cholesky PRIVATE -O3 -Xcompiler=-O3,-march=native,-Wall,-Wextra)\n\n# Link CUDA runtime and math library\ntarget_link_libraries(cholesky CUDA::cudart m)","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false}}
{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CfiRYTvS7baf8vi2Zu8rj","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The Cholesky benchmark now always runs on the GPU with CUDA, and at large sizes it runs close to the RTX 3090's FP64 speed limit. All changes are in `cholesky/cholesky.cpp` and `cholesky/CMakeLists.txt`; the executable is still `cholesky` and nothing is used beyond the CUDA runtime.\n\n**How it works**\n- **Algorithm:** a blocked Cholesky with 64-wide panels and four hand-written kernels: factor the 64×64 diagonal block, solve the panel below it, update the rest of the lower triangle, and zero the upper part. It doesn't use cuBLAS or cuSOLVER.\n- **Overlap:** the next panel's factorization runs on a high-priority stream while the rest of the update is still running.\n- **Copies:**\n  - The matrix goes to the GPU in growing row chunks and only the lower triangle is sent.\n  - Factorization starts on the first rows while later chunks are still copying; a separate stream brings each new chunk up to date with the panels already finished.\n  - Finished rows are copied back while computation continues.\n  - The host matrix is pinned outside the timed region.\n- **Same behaviour:** command-line options, output format and the `-r` results block are unchanged, and the upper triangle is zeroed. A matrix that isn't positive definite gives the same error message and index as before; I tested this with a bad diagonal at positions 0, 700 and 1500.\n- **Untimed parts:** the matrix-generation product and the L·Lᵀ check in validation also run on the GPU, so large sizes don't spend minutes in setup. Random numbers are still generated on the CPU with the same `rand_r` sequence.\n- **CMake:** the source is built as CUDA for the GPU in the machine (`native`), with `-O3 -march=native` passed to the host compiler.\n\n**Correctness:** all tested sizes pass `-v` (n = 0, 1, 7, 100, 513, 1000, 1031, 2047, 3000, 5000, 9001, among others). The worst relative error is about 1e-9, against a tolerance of 1e-6. The checksum in the results block matches the original exactly (tested at n = 1000, 1031 and 1600). The hash line differs, because summing in a different order changes the last bits.\n\n**Timing** (copies to and from the GPU are included in the timed region):\n\n| n | Original CPU | CUDA |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1000 | 235 ms | ~5 ms (n=1024) |\n| 2048 | – | 10 ms |\n| 4096 | – | 46 ms |\n| 8192 | – | 325 ms |\n| 16384 | – | ~2.4 s (≈570 GFLOPS) |\n\nAt n = 8192 that is about 89% of the ~628 GFLOP/s the GPU reaches on a long matrix multiply here. The main remaining loss is that the update kernels only get about 540 GFLOP/s.\n\n**One thing you might trip over:** CUDA 12 loads kernels lazily, and the first launch of a kernel waits for every copy already queued. That alone delayed the start by about 30 ms at n = 8192. The code now loads all kernels during setup; if you add a kernel, add it there too.\n\nThe program uses only one of the four GPUs. Splitting the work across all four could give up to about 4× more at large sizes. It would need a substantially more complex multi-GPU version, so I didn't attempt it."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":823,"cache_read_input_tokens":146635,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":823},"output_tokens":746,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"0662b794-5005-4748-a057-d5242925bb04","uuid":"9609b30d-53d3-4809-bb8d-e87efb2fe2ec","timestamp":"2026-10-05T04:01:50.010Z","request_id":"req_011CfiRYSe3GQMhwxFRPn4jG"}
